top10.descricao_en: Actively maintained ARTEX: AI autonomous penetration testing system. Self-hosted, model-agnostic, evidence-backed findings. Community continuation of Autumn-27/ARTEX, AGPL-3.0.
top10.readme:
# ARTEX
**Autonomous penetration testing that keeps its receipts.**
Self-hosted multi-agent offensive security. A planner explores, workers run real tools,
and every finding stays bound to the assets and HTTP traffic that prove it.
[ ](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/releases)
[ ](LICENSE)
[ ](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[ ](go.mod)
[ ](https://discord.gg/VKyvMTcgXh)
[Quick start](#quick-start) · [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Install](#installation) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [Security](SECURITY.md)
[ ](https://discord.gg/VKyvMTcgXh)
---
ARTEX is a self-hosted, LLM-driven penetration testing platform. It is not a chat wrapper around
a scanner: a planner splits a goal into intents, workers execute them with real tools, and the
results are written back into **two linked graphs**: one for what you know about the target, one
for how the test is progressing. Every finding can carry the captured request and response that
justify it, and every autonomous action passes through scope rules, approval gates and budgets.
- **It explores, it doesn't chat.** Goal decomposition, intent dispatch, worker execution and
  write-back form a closed loop that keeps advancing until the goal is proven.
- **Two graphs, one audit trail.** The shared asset graph says *what exists*; the per-task
  exploration graph says *what was tried, what it produced, and why*. Anchors link the two.
- **Findings with evidence.** A recording MITM proxy and a browser extension capture real traffic;
  findings, evidence quotes and retests are tied to the exact request/response.
- **Autonomy with brakes.** Human-in-the-loop approvals, argv-prefix rules, scope/deny gates,
  token and turn budgets, a target noise governor, and prompt-injection framing on tool output.
- **Self-hosted and model-agnostic.** One Go binary with the Next.js UI embedded, PostgreSQL,
  your own Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama.
---
## Quick start
```bash
git clone https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX.git
cd ARTEX
cp .env.example .env            # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD (and optionally an LLM key)
docker compose up -d --build    # builds from this checkout, starts PostgreSQL
```
Open **http://localhost:8787**. On the first visit `/setup` asks for the one-time setup token
printed at startup:
```bash
docker compose logs artex | grep "Setup token"
```
> Multi-arch release images (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) are published to GitHub Container
>

top10.descricao_en: Find the holes before someone else does. A fast, 100% Rust vulnerability scanner: XSS, SQL injection, leaked secrets, dependency CVEs and AI agent setups.
top10.readme:
safe-anything 
  Find the holes before someone else does.  
One command finds XSS, SQL injection and other vulnerabilities in your code, leaked secrets, 
risky mobile and cloud config, vulnerable dependencies, and the AI agent setup that writes it all. 
Every finding comes with the line, the reason and the fix. 
   Install   ·  Releases  ·  Claude Code plugin  ·  GitHub Action  ·  All 95 rules  ·  Agent setups  
Made in Türkiye 🇹🇷 by  erKam Yaman , who also made  rust-anything  ·  ❤️ Sponsor me  · Sponsored by  CodeRabbit  
   A real run on  OWASP Juice Shop  and on an agent setup with the usual mistakes (Apple M4).  What it finds on other repositories . 
       Your code  
      SQL and command injection, XSS,  eval , SSRF, path traversal, unsafe deserialization, weak crypto. Nine languages and SQL.
       Your secrets  
      Cloud and AI keys, tokens, private keys, passwords, and  .env  mistakes: committed env files, real values in  .env.example , secrets behind  NEXT_PUBLIC_  or  VITE_ . Always redacted in the output.
       Your stack  
      Android and iOS settings, Docker, GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, Terraform, nginx, and every locked dependency against OSV.dev.
       Your agent  
      MCP servers, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and OpenCode settings, hooks and skills: the files that decide what your agent may do.
## Quick start
```bash
cargo install safe-anything    # or: npx safe-anything .
safe-anything .
```
That's it. No config, no account, no upload. It exits with 1 when something high or critical is
found, so it works as a pre-commit or CI check as is.
```bash
safe-anything . --json             # machine-readable report
safe-anything . --sarif            # GitHub code scanning
safe-anything . --sarif-file out   # SARIF to the file out, the report on screen
safe-anything . --offline          # no network (skips the dependency check)
safe-anything . --severity medium  # hide low findings
safe-anything . --fail-on never    # always exit 0 (or low, medium, high, critical)
safe-anything . --include-tests    # also report findings in tests and fixtures
safe-anything --list-rules
```
- `.gitignore` is respected. List more paths in `.safe-anything-ignore`; it only adds to what is
  skipped, it cannot bring back what is listed below.
- These are never scanned, and the report only counts the files it did scan:
  - folders `.git`, `node_modules`, `target`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `.next`, `.venv`, `venv`,
    `__pycache__`, `Pods`, `.gradle` a

top10.descricao_en: Learn cloud security by building it! An open-source homelab teaching Zero Trust, DevSecOps, IaC, and cloud architecture from the ground up.
top10.readme:
# Clouds Against Humanity
A small, cheap, locked-down DigitalOcean environment built with OpenTofu, applied by Spacelift, fed secrets by Doppler, and reachable only through Twingate. **No droplet has a single public inbound port open.** There is no VPN, no bastion host and no SSH on the internet.
It is a cloud extension of a homelab, and it exists to teach: this repository is the reference environment, and the lessons that use it live in the wiki.
> ### Start with the wiki
>
> **The wiki is the real point of this project.** Every lesson, flowchart, exercise and decision (including the ones that were wrong the first time) is written there; this repository is the environment those lessons use.
>
> - **[Wiki home](https://github.com/ChiefGyk3D/Clouds-Against-Humanity/wiki)**: the map of everything.
> - **[Start here if you are new](https://github.com/ChiefGyk3D/Clouds-Against-Humanity/wiki/Start-Here-If-You-Are-New)**: cloud, Terraform and zero trust from zero.
> - **[Why this exists](https://github.com/ChiefGyk3D/Clouds-Against-Humanity/wiki/Why-This-Exists)**: where this comes from and who it is for.
> - **[Reading order](https://github.com/ChiefGyk3D/Clouds-Against-Humanity/wiki/Reading-Order)**: the paths, with time estimates.
> - **[Contents](https://github.com/ChiefGyk3D/Clouds-Against-Humanity/wiki/Contents)**: every page once, grouped by theme, with what each is for.
> - **[Git from zero](https://github.com/ChiefGyk3D/Clouds-Against-Humanity/wiki/Git-From-Zero)**: if you have never used git.
> - **[Repository growth](https://github.com/ChiefGyk3D/Clouds-Against-Humanity/wiki/Repository-Growth)**: stars, forks and weekly work, drawn from GitHub data; the as-of date is printed in the picture, and stars measure attention, not use.
>
> **Who this assumes:** a basic power user. You know how a computer works, may have built or repaired one, and have set up a router and done basic networking. If you could work a help desk or a retail repair counter, you can start; if not, [IT 101 level material such as CompTIA A+ objectives](https://github.com/ChiefGyk3D/Clouds-Against-Humanity/wiki/Start-Here-If-You-Are-New#where-zero-is) is the benchmark (not an endorsement).
>
> **Cost:** the reading and the exercises are free and always will be, and nothing here is sold. Hands-on work uses your own accounts and your provider's bill, nothing you spend goes to the maintainer, and you choose what you can afford to run. The cost gates are explained in [docs/cost.md](docs/cos

shirudo is a BPF-based security platform for Linux. After boot-time
initialization, it restricts BPF program loads from userspace to signed
loaders. Operators ship signed micropatches, called
[upatches](https://docs.shirudo.dev/upatches/learn/concepts.html),
and verify a target's measured upatch state with TPM-signed evidence.
shirudo (Japanese シールド, pronounced “shee-roo-doh”) means “shield”.
Read the announcements of shirudo on the blogs of
[OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/) and
[Cisco](https://isovalent.com/blog/post/cisco-openai-shirudo/).
## Quickstart
- [Try shirudo in a local VM](https://docs.shirudo.dev/start/quickstart.html).
  The VM uses a software TPM.
- [Read the documentation](https://docs.shirudo.dev/).
shirudo is pre-release. Production targets require a Linux kernel with
the signed-loader ABI and shirudo's kernel patches, plus a TPM 2.0. See the
[system requirements](https://docs.shirudo.dev/operate/plan/system-requirements.html).
CI runs all test tiers on x86-64 and host tests on arm64. The test VM
also boots locally on arm64. Target validation for riscv64 is pending.
The operator and target may use different architectures. See
[architecture support](https://docs.shirudo.dev/contribute/arch-support.html).
## Use cases
- **Runtime security and observability.** Observe process executions,
  network activity, and privilege changes with the included
  [`kernel-obs` package](upatches/kernel-obs/README.md).
- **Live mitigations.** Use BPF upatches to block vulnerable paths at kernel
  hooks or Java upatches to guard application code.
- **System hardening.** Use BPF upatches to enforce policies for
  containers, Kubernetes Pods, and LLM agents.
- **Embedded and edge devices.** Deliver signed mitigations to devices
  with long update cycles.
## Properties
- **Boot-time enforcement.** On production targets, enforcement starts
  when `shirudo init` attaches its guards from the initrd. The guards
  protect shirudo's runtime and state from root on the target without
  the operator's signing key.
- **Signed and sealed BPF.** BPF upatch loads and unloads go through
  loaders that the kernel verifies against the sealed `.bpf` keyring.
- **Signed Java agents.** shirudo verifies Java upatches in userspace.
  Configured JVMs load the agents at startup. See
  [Java agent upatches](https://docs.shirudo.dev/upatches/write/java-agents.html).

  per-boot TPM register. `shirudo a

# 全链哨兵 Full Chain Sentinel System
**简体中文** | [English](README.en.md) · **版本 2.3.5**
知攻善防实验室出品，基于 [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) 的授权渗透测试 Agent。通过中英文 Web 控制台，统一管理 Web、小程序与移动端测试、项目环境、审批和证据。
> **仅用于已获得书面授权的目标。** 自动执行模式可运行任意命令，使用者须自行承担操作后果。使用前请阅读[授权声明与安全边界](docs/security.md)。
[交流群](#community) · [快速开始](#quick-start) · [核心能力](#capabilities) · [常见问题 Q&A](#faq) · [文档导航](#documentation) · [许可](#license)
## 全链哨兵交流群
加入交流群请在打招呼内容中备注 **「全链哨兵」**。
[社区说明与致谢](docs/community.md)
---
## 快速开始
### 1. 下载并启动
先安装并启动 Docker，再从 [Releases](https://github.com/zgsfsec/Full-Chain-Sentinel-System/releases) 选择与你的系统和架构匹配的压缩包。
Linux x64 示例：
```sh
tar -xzf sentinel-web-linux-x64.tar.gz
cd sentinel-web
chmod +x sentinel-web
./sentinel-web
```
Windows 解压 `sentinel-web-windows-x64.zip` 后，在 PowerShell 运行 `.\sentinel-web.exe`。请保留程序旁的 `replayd/` 目录。
### 2. 完成初始化
打开启动日志中的**完整入口地址**，设置账号密码并确认授权声明。在「设置 → 环境」准备工具镜像，在「设置 → 模型」添加端点并分配主模型，然后创建项目。
新项目包含工作容器与常驻网关，切换代理无需重建工作容器。
### 3. 开始测试
在对话中描述授权范围和目标，默认使用审批模式。移动端测试需先接入设备，再启用当前会话的对应工具。
[安装部署与启动参数](docs/deployment.md) · [源码运行](docs/deployment.md#section-3) · [使用指南](docs/usage.md) · [设备接入](docs/mobile.md)
---
## 核心能力
以下截图来自源码运行的完整控制台，使用独立本地项目、真实后端与 Docker 容器。报告模板相关截图更新至 **v2.3.4**，其余截图保留各自记录的版本；没有记录或未接入设备的页面按实际状态展示。[截图来源与更新方式](images/screenshots/README.md)。
### 1. 项目概览
汇总当前项目的运行任务、待审批项、漏洞与会话；从最近会话、运行状态和漏洞分布进入具体工作。
### 2. 对话与持续目标
流式展示回复、思考与工具过程，支持会话分支、文件、终端和子代理。在输入区选择审批模式、预设 Agent、监督及设备工具；持续目标在自动执行或 AI 审批模式下续跑。
### 3. 项目与代理
项目隔离工作目录、容器、会话与漏洞记录。新项目使用 Kali 工作容器和常驻网关；代理页管理 SOCKS5/HTTP、订阅、WireGuard 与 OpenVPN，运行中的项目可切换出口。
 查看界面截图 
### 4. 漏洞与资产库
在漏洞页筛选、复核严重程度、CVSS、状态与证据，导出 Markdown 报告；资产库按项目归并域名、IP、服务和 URL，维护标签、测试记录与关联漏洞。
 查看界面截图 
### 5. MITM 中心
为当前项目启动 HTTP 显式代理、安装 HTTPS 解密证书，实时查看流量。按方法和状态筛选，检查请求与响应，并将选中的数据包发送到 WebFuzz。
 查看界面截图 
### 6. WebFuzz 发包工作台
多标签编辑原始 HTTP 请求，选择项目代理、直连或 MITM 路由，查看响应报文、正文和响应头，检索响应内容并回看历史。下图为真实请求本地文档服务得到的 200 响应。
### 7. 业务建模
让 Agent 给项目的业务留下一份模型，一次建模一条记录，在项目内查看状态、范围与两部分的计数，打开详情或导出。记录分两部分，每部分依据什么由 Agent 按手上的输入决定：**接口文档**——一份 OpenAPI 3.0 文档加业务实体，有流量时从实际响应还原，只有源码时按源码里声明的接口写；**读源码**——工作目录里有源码时，为代码审计提交每个接口的调用链、权限校验位置、读写的表，以及状态机、资源归属等业务规则（每条结论带代码位置，控制台不核对位置是否真实存在）。所有 Agent 都能读本项目已有的记录；工程模式下指挥官可以把「做业务建模」写进任务指令派发给执行 Agent。
 查看界面截图 
### 8. POC 库与订阅
检索和引用 Nuclei 模板；在「设置 → POC 订阅」管理官方或自建订阅源、同步计划和更新记录。模板同步与执行测试是不同操作。
手动同步、同步官方和定时同步均使用同步开始时当前项目的代理网络，重试不会跟随切换后的其他项目。未选择项目或项目不使用代理时，走宿主机网络；项目代理不可用时记录同步失败，不自动直连。订阅与模板库仍全局共享。
 查看界面截图 
### 9. 开源情报
批量添加 GitHub / GitHub Enterprise 仓库和分支，按固定间隔或 Cron 监控新提交。动态页集中处理安全更新、判定失败与检查异常，支持复现、重判、忽略与日志回溯；复现会准备漏洞版和修
